newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish 96 budget spending up to FIM 201 bln -govt.
newsitem.headline: Finnish 96 budget spending up to FIM 201 bln -govt.

text.p: The Finnish government said in a statement on Tuesday its supplementary budget due to go to parliament on Friday will increase total 1996 state budget spending to 201.3 billion markka.
The statement did not give a comparison.
The supplementary budget will raise expenditure by 6.85 billion markka, the government said. "Total spending budgeted for 1996 will rise to 201.3 billion markka," it said.

The supplementary budget will require an increase in 1996 state net borrowing of 3.6 billion markka. The full-year net borrowing requirement to cover budget spending would be a "lower than expected" 38.9 billion markka, the statement said.
Total 1996 net borrowing to cover the deficit of the state finances would be "exactly 43 billion markka, more or less", finance ministry budget chief Erkki Virtanen told Reuters.
This is a revision downwards from 44.7 billion.
Including expenditure items outside the budget, total 1996 state sending will be around 213 billion markka, the finance ministry said earlier.
In January-August, state net borrowing totalled 41.28 billion markka, according to State Treasury Office figures.
In 1995, state net borrowing was about 56 billion markka.
